In the above extracted JavaScript, the unescaped content looks particularly interesting. This must be the shellcode that will be injected. So it was decoded using this recipe in the [Cyberchef.](https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef/#recipe=Find_/_Replace(%7B'option':'Regex','string':'%25u'%7D,'',true,false,true,false)Swap_endianness('Hex',2,true)From_Hex('Auto')&&oeol=FF) 

![Decoding unescaped content](/images/2025-01-18-Flare-On-2014-C4/1.png)

The above decoded content now looks like a shellcode with some barely visible Windows API like `LoadLibraryA`. The shellcode was then saved to a file named `shellcode.bin`.

The shellcode was converted into executable using [shcode2exe](https://github.com/accidentalrebel/shcode2exe) as:
```
python3 shcode2exe.py ../shellcode.bin -o shellcode.exe
```

The output `shellcode.exe` executable was loaded into **x32dbg**. Since `LoadLibraryA` was seen earlier and is commonly used by shellcode to load required modules. So, a breakpoint was set on it.
```
bp LoadLibraryA
```

Then
